about: The thumbnail prompt library for marketing-thumbnail: house-prompt blocks 1-11, the identity lock, 11 expressions, alternate takes, split frames, surgical tweaks, the 3D-logo prompt, the 16 concept frameworks and the bake checklists. Every row is SL8's restatement of the Higgsfield thumbnail skill (no licence stated, copied false), cited by research id in `from`; rows with `from: null` are SL8-written and name their basis. scripts/thumb.mjs fills the {placeholders}; never edit a row inside a job. The wording has not been run on SL8's fal route.

rows.prompt: Make a loud, scroll-stopping YouTube thumbnail composite in {ratio}: photoreal, poster-quality and high-energy, never a subdued film still. Keep it one seamless picture with no split screen and no diagonal division, every element flowing across one continuous shot.
On the tall canvas, frame the subject so faces sit within the top two-thirds.
On the tall canvas, place the main subject within the top two-thirds.
Render everything in precisely the medium the style key names: {medium}.
This is not photorealism and contains no real photographs.

Carry every character into this medium with its design intact; keep the main subject, the safe area, the palette and legibility at feed size, and never turn an illustrated character into a photographic face.
SCENE (show it exactly as written): {scene}.
Leave the image free of lettering, legible interface labels and watermarks.

TEXT: a bold headline rendered into the image that reads exactly "{text}", in huge, highly legible sans-serif lettering with a crisp outline or glow, positioned so it never sits over a face. Nothing else written, and no watermark.

BAKED UI: a {ui_kind} showing exactly "{ui_text}" in plain, generic interface styling, with no real brand, app or broadcaster named or shown. Keep the wording brief and faithful to what the video shows.

IDENTITY LOCK for CHARACTER {n}, the person shown in face reference #{k}: render this same individual so the face matches the photo, with an identical bone structure and eye shape and the same nose, lips, jawline, hairline, hair texture and skin tone. Do not flatter, blend with other faces or restyle the face; anyone who knows them should recognise them instantly. Expression: {expression}.
CHARACTER {n}, from reference #{k}: keep this character's design exactly (shapes, proportions, colours, costume) and draw it in the medium above. Expression: {expression}.
rows.basis: research:higgsfield/thumbnailgeneration-e3191f#46; research:WF13-a2 step 12 (character-design lock in the non-photoreal handoff)

rows.prompt: PERSON {n}: {description}. Expression: {expression}.

Show the subject BIG and commanding as the obvious hero, taking up roughly half the frame (40-60%), shot from the chest up or as a medium close-up, brought forward and clearly separated from what is behind it; never a tiny figure low in the frame and never a far-off look like a grabbed video still.
Every face is in sharp focus and anchors the image.
KEY ELEMENTS (the signature props or effects that make the image jump out): {elements}.
{noun}, shown oversized and hurtling toward the lens

LOGO: the supplied logo set into the picture exactly as given, its shapes, colours and proportions untouched, placed cleanly in 2D at a strong focal point with a light drop shadow to lift it, never over a face.

LOGO: the supplied 3D logo render placed in the scene as a real solid object, its glossy dimensional surface picking up the scene's key and rim light and throwing a soft contact shadow, set at a strong focal point clear of every face.
LOCATION (where it is, the hour, the weather and the mood): {location}.
COMPOSITION: {composition}.

the subject shown BIG and dominant, from the chest up or as a medium close-up, taking up roughly half the frame (40-60%), set forward on a power third and shot from eye level, cleanly separated from the background so it stands out, with shallow depth of field and a foreground accent
BACKGROUND (blended, never split): {background}.
a bold, vivid gradient of saturated colour in strong, high-contrast tones that echo the subject's palette, with a soft vignette and falloff toward the edges

LIGHTING: YouTube-thumbnail lighting on the subject, with a powerful KEY LIGHT modelling the face, sharp highlights and a controlled roll-off; a DREAM LIGHT fill, soft and dreamy, raising the shadows with a faint glow; and a clear BACK LIGHT and HAIR LIGHT drawing a bright rim along hair, shoulders and outline so the subject separates sharply from the background.
rows.from: higgsfield/thumbnailgeneration-e3191f@Block 10 Lighting rig, colored rim variant and rim palette

rows.prompt: LIGHTING: YouTube-thumbnail lighting on the subject, with a powerful KEY LIGHT modelling the face, sharp highlights and a controlled roll-off; a DREAM LIGHT fill, soft and dreamy, raising the shadows with a faint glow; and a clear {color} BACK LIGHT and HAIR LIGHT drawing a vivid coloured edge along hair, shoulders and outline, with a faint glow in the same colour. The key and fill stay neutral; only the back and hair lights take the colour.
rows.from: higgsfield/thumbnailgeneration-e3191f@Block 10 Lighting rig, colored rim variant and rim palette

rows.prompt: GRADE: a vivid, high-impact grade with hard contrast, a bright and clean exposure, deep saturated colour that leaps off the screen, inky blacks against bright highlights and a crisp glossy finish with poster punch, all reading as one unified image. Frame: {ratio}.
IMAGE REFERENCES: {list}.
jaw open in a gasp, eyes wide
beaming ecstatic smile, fiery eyes
petrified stare, holding its breath
a single eyebrow lifted, baffled
clenched jaw, intense focus
self-satisfied, knowing half-grin
steady magnetic gaze, easy brows, the slightest poised half-smile; leading-man assurance, confident and never aggressive
pulling back in a grimace of revulsion
mouth fallen open, eyes shining with wonder
teeth bared in fury
head thrown back laughing

ALTERNATE TAKE: recompose as a hero shot from below, the camera under eye level angled upward, the subject looming with added power and the background's lines rising up, with the scene and light unchanged.
ALTERNATE TAKE: a tight close-up push-in in which face and expression fill over half the frame and the background is squeezed into soft out-of-focus context, with the scene and light unchanged.

ALTERNATE TAKE: a wider, more kinetic angle with a slight Dutch tilt, more of the surroundings in view, the subject set off-centre on a power third and a stronger sense of motion sweeping across, with the scene and light unchanged.
SPLIT-FRAME thumbnail in {ratio}: the image is cut into {count} {panels} along clean, strong seams; each panel is a complete small scene of its own, and one premium grade runs through every panel.
Each panel carries one side of the story: {panels_desc}.
LEFT panel: how things were BEFORE, {before}. RIGHT panel: how they are AFTER, {after}. Make the two states of this one change contrast as sharply as possible.
Each panel shows a single contender, staged and lit like a fight-night poster: {panels_desc}. Give both the same visual weight, with face-off tension across the seam.
Put no labels, captions, words or numbers on the panels or between them; the comparison must work through images alone. Grade every panel as one premium picture.

Alter the facial expression of the person, and only that, to: {phrase}. Keep the identity, face shape, hair, clothing, body, pose, background, logo, composition and lighting exactly as they are, faithful to every pixel. Do not touch the thumbnail lighting rig.

Swap out the background, and only the background, for: {phrase}. The subject, their face, identity, clothing, pose, the logo and everything in the foreground stay exactly the same. Re-light the edges of the subject so they match where the new backdrop's light comes from, its colour and its rim, and read naturally; the YouTube rig stays.

Recolour the background ONLY, moving its palette to mostly {phrase} tones. Its layout, contents and depth stay exactly as they are. Refresh the faint ambient colour spill along the subject's outline, and leave the key and fill light on the face untouched.

Change only the colour of the rim light (the back and hair light, the bright edge along hair, shoulders and outline) to {phrase}. Leave key and fill light alone, and leave the background, identity, pose, logo, clothing and composition as they are.

Turn the supplied flat logo into a high-end 3D render: extrude its exact shapes into glossy solid volumes while every letter, proportion and brand colour stays EXACT, with a premium CGI product finish (soft studio reflections, fine bevels, sharp edges), floating over a plain dark neutral studio backdrop and a soft contact shadow beneath. Centred with generous margins; no added text and no watermark.

Look at the style reference yourself and write work/

/reference.json with these keys: brief (the concept in one dense sentence), subject (pose and action in general terms, never who it is), person_count (0-3), emotion (a preset name from the 11, else other), emotion_detail (a single vivid sentence on eyes, brows, mouth and head angle), composition, background, location, elements, split (true or false), split_count.
Follow how the reference frames its shot.

Want a recurring character on the thumbnail? Send its character image and its look will be locked; otherwise say whether you want a generated person or no people at all. A photo of a real person cannot be used yet: SL8 is still approving the consent text it needs.

Before any paid call: the route is the one this skill names for the call; block 1 (or its split or medium replacement) opens the prompt and GRADE closes it whenever block 11 applies; a person in frame has the lighting block and one identity lock per face photo (a non-photoreal handoff uses its medium and design lock and no photographic lighting); the style reference is not among the --ref files; each call makes exactly one image; without ordered text the no-lettering line is present; the quote for the whole plan fits the budget.
Before and after: the split frame in before-after mode, making one subject's starting and finished states as different as possible.
Social interface: KEY ELEMENTS is a message bubble, DM line or star-rating card in generic styling next to the subject, its short message carried by BAKED UI; no real platform's branding.
Three steps: a split frame of three upright panels (plain or custom mode) showing the start, a middle beat and the end; a number or Day badge per panel is optional.
Real screenshot: no generation. Take an actual frame from the customer's video, or stage an action shot that matches its opening frame; say so when the customer has a clip.
Posed portrait (the default): the subject BIG in frame with the identity lock, the YouTube lighting and an expression, and little or nothing behind them, because the subject is the point.
Posed action: the scene is one intriguing action caught mid-movement; keep the composition uncluttered around that single action.
A specific day: any framework plus a large DAY N badge through BAKED UI; choose a day from roughly the final fifth of the story.
Graphic: not photoreal. Swap the frame block for a clean diagram brief (a bell curve or another simple, familiar chart) and leave out the photoreal and lighting blocks.
Landscape: the place is the hero, with one small subject kept on a power third; the lighting block is optional.
Map or aerial: the picture is a map or a photo from above, and KEY ELEMENTS marks a route or point (a circle, an arrow, a label through BAKED UI).
Product: the product is the SUBJECT, sharp and heroic, its own label left as it is; the curiosity comes from the product turning out to be what the title asks about.
Text: the deterministic overlay by default, or in-render TEXT when ordered; it works as a pointer (an arrow plus one word), or it picks up where the title leaves off, or answers it.
Repetition: KEY ELEMENTS is a huge number of a single object crowding the picture yet still readable, plus one context element and a subject to show scale.
Size difference: the composition sets two story-critical elements at wildly different scales, huge against tiny.
News clip: a generic breaking-news lower-third or ticker across the image (BAKED UI, one short true line), styled like no real broadcaster.
Amplified reality: a staged action shot that exaggerates one real element of the story (an oversized KEY ELEMENT) and stays believable, since overdoing it loses trust.

Whatever the framework, the underlying rules hold: one clear focal subject, a real information gap, strong contrast that still reads at about 120 px, emotion or intrigue on every face, nothing cluttered, honesty about the video, and an idea grasped in less than a second in a busy feed.

Headline look: Anton (a heavy condensed sans) in one weight; ALL CAPS; a thick stroke, 8-14% of the cap height, painted beneath the fill; a hard dark shadow pushed downward; one loud colour (white, a yellow-to-orange-to-red fire gradient, or acid lime #D4FF3F); tight tracking (-0.01 to -0.02 em) and line height 0.9.

A headline of two to four words, never a sentence; kept off the face in an empty quarter (bottom, a corner or a side); big, with a cap height of 12-18% of the frame's height, larger when unsure; inside the frame with comfortable padding, away from the very edges.

Before baking: Anton, ALL CAPS, two to four words; a thick stroke painted under the fill; nothing over the face, the headline in an empty quarter; inside the frame, clear of the edges; one loud colour per headline; the font confirmed before drawing (the bake script checks fc-match and glyph coverage first).
Another family: pass --font with the family and --weight; the stroke, shadows, paint order and tracking stay as the style defines them, and nothing changes except the family and its weight.
